items.title: FPGA bitstream documentation
items.goal: Complete, machine-readable bitstream databases for every commercial off-the-shelf FPGA family
items.frame: The FPGA's equivalent of a PDK: the device database every open FPGA tool builds on. Moves FPGA documentation from manual reverse engineering to automated fuzzing and checking.

items.title: Open "almost manufacturable" PDKs
items.goal: Realistic open PDKs at 55/45nm, 28/22nm and 16/12nm pre-EUV FinFET, with consistency audits and generated docs
items.frame: The foundation layer: open PDKs come first because they make open tools and open IP possible. Covers bulk and FinFET nodes.

items.title: Design rule checking (DRC)
items.goal: Per-rule tests, sourced reasons and a rule-deck audit for SKY130, GF180MCU and SG13G2, plus a distributed DRC engine
items.frame: Straddles two layers: rule decks, tests and rule docs belong to the PDK, while the distributed engine is tooling.

items.title: Open TCAD stack
items.goal: Process and device simulation that reproduces an existing open PDK from its process description
items.frame: PDK layer: generates the device models a PDK ships, from process physics instead of foundry data.

items.title: Adder and multiplier exploration
items.goal: Generate and characterise many arithmetic architectures per node so open synthesis picks the best one
items.frame: An IP generator for custom computation, plus synthesis changes so tools pick the right architecture. Moves arithmetic from hand-picked designs to generated, characterised ones.

items.title: Reproducible and signed toolchain
items.goal: Bit-identical tool builds and outputs, with every tool, PDK and artefact signed and logged
items.frame: Tooling that underpins every other tool: trustworthy, repeatable builds for ASIC and FPGA flows alike.

items.title: Composable and distributed simulation
items.goal: Swap Renode, Verilator or FPGA emulation per SoC block, and scale the model across a cluster
items.frame: Verification and simulation tooling that cuts across interface, computation and storage blocks.

items.title: Standard cell generation
items.goal: Generate, characterise and verify complete cell libraries for any PDK, voltage and track height
items.frame: The PDK's "primitives and low-level data": a cell generator rather than a hand-drawn library, which is the manual-to-automated shift.

items.title: Toolchain verification
items.goal: Per-stage checks that each open FPGA and ASIC tool's output is correct, so failures point at their cause
items.frame: Tooling quality: checks every stage of both ASIC and FPGA flows.

items.title: Accelerator interface and harness
items.goal: One accelerator interface, as a LiteX FPGA flavour and a Sea2sky-style ASIC harness sharing host software
items.frame: IP joining interface and computation: one accelerator interface with an FPGA focus (LiteX) and an ASIC focus (Sea2sky-style harness).

items.title: FPGA benchmarking
items.goal: Continuous benchmark of open FPGA toolchains against themselves on real boards, with seed statistics, kept as an AI training corpus
items.frame: Measurement tooling for the FPGA side: scores the open FPGA tool and device stack.

items.title: ASIC benchmarking
items.goal: Re-runnable benchmark of open ASIC flows against themselves on every open shuttle design, kept as an AI training corpus
items.frame: Measurement tooling for the ASIC side: scores PDKs, tools and IP together.

items.title: FPGA Interchange and open place and route
items.goal: Revive FPGA Interchange and make VPR and nextpnr better release over release, measured open against open
items.frame: FPGA tooling: the FPGA counterpart of open ASIC place and route.

items.title: Incremental toolchains
items.goal: FPGA and ASIC flows where a small change costs a small rebuild, identical to a full one
items.frame: Tooling speed for both ASIC and FPGA flows.

items.title: Fully open FPGA and eFPGA
items.goal: An open FPGA and eFPGA architecture, hardened with open tools, improving generation over generation
items.frame: An IP generator for the deck's flexibility-critical computation: an eFPGA block in ASICs and a standalone FPGA.

items.title: Open high-speed connectivity IP
items.goal: Open PCIe, USB 3, Ethernet and DDR controllers and PHYs that work on FPGAs and in ASICs
items.frame: Interface IP (digital controllers and analog PHYs): the deck's interconnect and memory-interface "uncore".

items.title: Open MPW tapeout programs
items.goal: Recurring open shuttles whose designs and silicon results build a library of proven IP and benchmarks
items.frame: Sits outside the three layers: real silicon is the proof that the PDK, tooling and IP layers work.

items.title: Replicating classic ASIC and FPGA papers
items.goal: Reproduce key past papers and test whether their conclusions hold with AI and fast compute
items.frame: Measurement: re-tests past results across tooling, IP and process questions.

items.title: Libraries for every EDA file format
items.goal: Well-tested readers and writers for every open EDA format, and proprietary ones with a public description, shared by all tools
items.frame: Foundation of the tooling layer: shared readers and writers so every ASIC and FPGA tool speaks every format.

items.title: Partial hardening
items.goal: Harden only the critical high-performance core as ASIC, with the rest in eFPGA and software on CPUs
items.frame: Embodies the deck's criticality scale in one chip: performance-critical hard core, flexibility-critical eFPGA, non-critical software.

items.title: Open wireless with eFPGA and SDR
items.goal: Open LoRa, NFC, Bluetooth, WiFi and cellular stacks with open RF front ends and baseband in eFPGA and software
items.frame: Interface IP: the deck's wireless "uncore", with analog RF front ends and a flexible eFPGA and software baseband.

items.title: Virtual foundry in the cloud
items.goal: Simulate every process step and recipe of a fab, and its effect on devices, yield and fab operations
items.frame: PDK layer, one level below the PDK itself: the process a PDK comes from. Moves process development from wafers inside a few companies to open, automated simulation.

items.title: Non-rectilinear layout tooling
items.goal: Open layout tools, rules and cells for hexagonal, octagonal, diagonal and curved geometry, measured against Manhattan flows
items.frame: Tooling layer, with the PDK's rules and cells beneath it: a layout stack not tied to the Manhattan grid. Breaks the loop where rules, cells and tools only support right angles because that is all anyone has built for.

gaps: **Storage has no item.** The memory compilers candidate (SRAM, register file, ROM) would fill it.
**Analog interface is thin.** Only open-links' PHYs and open-airwaves' RF front ends touch it; the analog generators candidate fills the rest.
**CPUs have no item.** This is deliberate: open RISC-V cores are plentiful, and the gaps are in the layers around them.
**Tooling dominates,** by choice: open PDKs and tools are what make open IP possible.
